title: Signal and Static
premise: Sebastian Ravensworth, a terraformer tending a garden world seeded for colonists two centuries from now, runs supply routes between settlements that severed contact after the Silence—a collapse of the interstellar relay network. When her aging ship intercepts a distress signal broadcast in a language extinct since the Silence, she realizes someone at the edge of dead space is alive, and that the signal is a key: proof the Silence was engineered, not accidental. Racing a failing reactor and a corporate salvage fleet that wants the evidence destroyed, Sebastian reaches the derelict relay and finds its last keeper—a dying archivist who preserved the truth at the cost of her own memories. To carry the signal home, Sebastian must sacrifice the terraformed garden's power core, dooming the unborn colonists' paradise to save the living's right to justice, and she chooses the living.
about_author: Hazel Eastwick is the pen name of a former radio engineer who spent a decade maintaining remote transmission stations in the Arctic before turning to fiction. Her work blends hard technical detail with elegiac prose, exploring what survives when institutions fail.

chapters.title: The Garden of the Unborn
chapters.summary: Sebastian tends the terraforming arrays on Meridian, a world seeded for colonists who won't arrive for two hundred years. Her POV establishes her isolation, her ritual of recording messages for people not yet born, and the quiet ache of a life spent serving a future she'll never see. Beat: tender loneliness.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Sebastian pilots her freighter, the Kestrel's Wake, between three silent settlements that stopped speaking to each other after the Silence. Through her eyes we see the decayed relay buoys and the barter economy of survivors. She delivers seed stock and takes on a passenger: a cynical salvager named Okafor. Beat: wary companionship.

chapters.title: A Voice in Extinct Tongues
chapters.summary: In deep transit, the Kestrel's Wake catches a repeating signal in High Meridian Standard—officially extinct for two centuries. Sebastian, who learned it from her grandmother's archives, is the only living translator. Okafor urges her to ignore it; dead signals mean dead ships and scavenger fleets. Beat: dread and irresistible curiosity.

chapters.title: What the Silence Buried
chapters.summary: Decoding fragments, Sebastian realizes the signal contains timestamps proving the relay network was deliberately collapsed—not failed. Her POV flashes to her grandmother, a network technician erased from official records. The signal is triangulating from the Vesper Relay, at the edge of dead space. Beat: the personal becomes political.

chapters.title: The Salvage Fleet
chapters.summary: Okafor's old contacts warn that the Halcyon Combine's salvage fleet has also detected the signal and is moving to erase it. Sebastian must choose: return to her garden and safety, or run the long route to Vesper. She commits, and Okafor, reluctantly, stays aboard. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: Port in a Dead Orbit
chapters.summary: At the lawless station of Threnody, Sebastian trades her cargo of garden seeds for reactor fuel—sacrificing part of Meridian's future to fund the journey. A Combine agent, Ilsa Vane, offers to buy her silence. Her refusal marks her. Beat: the price of principle, made literal.

chapters.title: Okafor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV reveals his own history: his family died in a Combine 'relocation' after the Silence, and he's spent years pretending neutrality. He nearly sells Sebastian out to Vane for a pardon, then burns the offer. Beat: guilt, temptation, and a quiet turn toward loyalty.

chapters.title: Static on the Long Route
chapters.summary: Pursued by a Combine corvette, Sebastian threads the debris fields of the old relay chain, using her grandmother's unpublished routing codes—knowledge the Combine believes destroyed. The chase costs the ship's long-range antenna. Beat: exhilarating survival through inherited knowledge.

chapters.title: The Archive of Small Voices
chapters.summary: Sheltering in a hollowed relay buoy, Sebastian and Okafor find thousands of recorded final messages from the Silence's victims—people who understood what was happening and spoke into the dark. Sebastian recognizes her grandmother's voice among them. Beat: grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Vane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Vane boards the buoy under truce and offers Sebastian truth without justice: the Combine will let her live if she surrenders the decoded signal. Sebastian counters by broadcasting one victim's message on open channels—forcing Vane's crew to hear what they're complicit in. Beat: moral jiu-jitsu; a seed of doubt in the enemy.

chapters.title: Edge of Dead Space
chapters.summary: The final leg: no fuel stations, no beacons, reactor degrading. Okafor's POV as he hand-welds the damaged antenna during a micrometeorite storm, nearly dying. They cross into dead space where the signal grows strong and clear. Beat: endurance, and the strange comfort of the growing signal.

chapters.title: The Vesper Relay
chapters.summary: They reach Vesper: a cathedral of dead machinery still faintly alive. Inside, automated systems greet them in High Meridian Standard—the first voice of their own language Sebastian has heard in months. Something is still maintaining the relay. Beat: awe and unease.

chapters.title: The Keeper
chapters.summary: They find the source: Maren Sol, the relay's last technician, kept alive for decades by the station's failing medical systems, her own memories eroded by the same treatment. She has spent her life preserving the proof of the engineered Silence. Beat: meeting a ghost who chose memory over self.

chapters.title: What Maren Remembered
chapters.summary: Maren's fragmented POV: memories surfacing in wrong order—the order to collapse the network, the colleagues who complied, the archives she hid inside the relay's core. She no longer remembers her own face but remembers every timestamp. Beat: memory as the last territory of the self.

chapters.title: The Combine Arrives
chapters.summary: Vane's corvette docks at Vesper with orders to scuttle the station. Sebastian, Okafor, and the frail Maren have hours to extract the archive before the Combine cuts the core. Okafor volunteers to hold the docking ring. Beat: siege begins, clock running.

chapters.title: Holding the Ring
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV: he fights not to win but to delay, using every salvage trick he knows, buying minutes with blood. He finally faces Vane directly and speaks his family's name into the record—making her complicity personal. Beat: a man atoning in real time.

chapters.title: The Archive and the Cost
chapters.summary: The archive is stored in the relay's power core; extraction will drain it. Sebastian realizes the only portable power source is the Kestrel's drive core—the same core that powers Meridian's terraforming array. Taking it dooms the garden's timeline. Beat: the central sacrifice crystallizes.

chapters.title: Maren's Choice
chapters.summary: Maren reveals the archive can broadcast itself once—on a carrier wave that will reach every surviving settlement—if the relay's full power is spent. But the relay's power comes from Vesper's core, and spending it kills her life support. She chooses the broadcast. Beat: the keeper completes her vigil.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: As the Combine breaches the station, Sebastian triggers the transmission: two centuries of suppressed truth, in a language rising from extinction, flooding every open channel. Vane's crew hears their own victims. Vane hesitates—and her hesitation lets them live. Beat: catharsis; justice spoken, not won by force.

chapters.title: After the Signal
chapters.summary: Maren dies as the relay goes dark, her last recorded words a message for the unborn. Sebastian and Okafor escape in the crippled Kestrel's Wake, carrying Maren's personal archive and the knowledge that the settlements are listening to each other again. Beat: mourning braided with hope.

chapters.title: The Garden, Replanted
chapters.summary: Sebastian returns to Meridian with a drained core and a changed mission: the garden will grow slower, wilder, on solar trickle instead of the core—but the first response signals from other worlds are arriving, and colonists may come in fifty years instead of two hundred. Beat: loss measured against a nearer future.

chapters.title: Signal, Not Static
chapters.summary: Epilogue: Sebastian records a new message for the unborn—this time telling them the truth about how their world was nearly traded away, and who paid. Okafor tends the arrays beside her; the sky fills with returning voices. The long route between worlds is open again. Beat: quiet, earned resolution.
